meta.title: About — {name}
meta.description: About {name}: mechanical engineering education, internship experience in rehabilitation engineering, and professional goals in assistive technology.

introduction.primary: A mechanical engineer who designs with people, not just for them.
introduction.secondary: I'm {name}, a mechanical engineer focused on assistive technology. I enjoy the moment a device stops being a prototype and becomes part of someone's daily routine.

background.title: Background
paragraphs: My interest in accessibility began when I helped adapt a family member's wheelchair and realised how few products are designed around the individual. Since then I have focused my studies and internships on rehabilitation engineering.

During my internships I worked alongside occupational therapists, clinicians and wheelchair users — running interviews, defining requirements, modelling in CAD, analysing parts and fabricating prototypes in the workshop.
I care about devices that are robust, light, affordable and easy to maintain, and about documenting them clearly so others can build on the work.

entries.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern
entries.body: Designed and tested custom wheelchair adaptations with clinicians and users; produced manufacturing drawings and FEA reports.

entries.title: Product Design Intern
entries.body: Developed parametric 3D-printed assistive grips and trained therapists to customise and print them in-house.

entries.title: MEng Mechanical Engineering
entries.body: Focus on mechanical design, biomechanics and product development. Final-year project in assistive mobility.

goals.title: Professional goals
goals.lead: I'm looking to join a product development or rehabilitation engineering team where I can take assistive devices from user research through to manufacture — and keep learning from the people who use them.
